note: Price transclusions that already read as vendor attributions when the price-attribution check was written (beads addictedtoai-l6j). Each is a DEBT, not an exemption: it warns on every build and fails the moment a new one appears. This list has one legal direction, down. Repair is the clause the corpus uses -- that the figure is the top listed provider's rate for that row rather than necessarily that company's own -- or a reword to what the listing does ("the row lists at"). Never name the provider: it rotates. sdh swept and fixed six other files by hand; these four it never looked at.

repaid.note: All 15 recorded debts repaid; the list reached the empty state build-content.mjs calls "the state the file is supposed to reach". Nothing was withdrawn. Before repairing, every ratio the four files assert was re-derived from the LIVE per-provider endpoint lists (https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models/<row>/endpoints, 22 rows, all HTTP 200, fetched 2026-08-31) rather than from the headline alone, because two of these were suspected INVERTED rather than merely unhedged. They were not: on every one of the 22 rows the snapshot headline equals the vendor's own standard-tier endpoint rate, so all thirteen ratios (the 12x Pro premium on GPT-5/5.2/5.4, the 6x on 5.5, the 1x on all three GPT-5.6 variants, the 10x Sol-to-Luna gap, and Opus 4.7-fast 6x / 4.8-fast 2x / 5-fast 2x) hold identically at the vendor's own rate. The repair is therefore additive and no claim changed value. Each of the four files was repaired twice over: the attributing verb was replaced with a listing verb AND the house hedge added, so zero sentences depend on the section-wide hedge exemption -- which matters here because none of these bodies carries an ATX heading, so sectionAround() spans the whole file and one stray "provider" would otherwise have silenced it.
repaid.residual_hazard: addictedtoai-pfc -- the fetch also showed the headline is one SERVICE TIER among several the SAME provider lists for the row (openai/flex at 0.5x, openai standard at 1x, openai/fast at 2x; google-ai-studio/flex 1x/2x/3.6x priority; azure/eu and azure/us at +10%). So "OpenAI charges $2/M" is under-specified even when OpenAI is the top provider and the check is satisfied. Not modelled by lib/price-attribution.mjs and out of scope for sng.
